'''Use rule:''' distinguish death, will-making, decree and confirmation dates. A testament dative is a court administration, not a statement of the deceased's wishes. A same-name person in the same county is not an identification, and a spouse is not automatically the named children's other parent.

== Ninian Glasgow and later proposed branches ==

[[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow (about 1550–1613)]] was a '''fisher and burgess''', not a flesher. His 1613 testament directly names [[Glasgow-1027|Robert]] as his son, John as his brother and [[Glasgow-3062|Marion]] as his sister. His then wife was Jonet Hutchesoun; a separate testament establishes that earlier wife Jonet Meik was Robert's mother. Damaged wording does not safely prove William or Elizabeth as further children.

The following later testaments remain important but should not be indented as a proved descent from Ninian:

* John Glasgow, merchant burgess, died September 1635; spouse Jonet Wilson; the testament names sons Robert, William and Ninian and daughters Margaret and Jonet. [[Glasgow-1561]] is only a possible identity: its sourced baptisms place a same-name father at Linlithgow, but no inspected record yet joins him to this Glasgow merchant household.
* [[Glasgow-3075|William Glasgow]], mealmaker in Leith, died September 1645; [[Glasgow-3078|Archibald Glasgow]] is independently proved as his son, but William's placement beneath Ninian remains uncertain.
* [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow]], indweller in Quothquan, died February 1650; spouse Marioun Cok and lawful sister Bessie are established, while proposed sons and identification of [[Glasgow-1086|a later Quothquan John]] require separate proof.

== Edinburgh Commissary Court rural households ==
* [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow]], whose estate was processed on 4 May 1577
** ''Widow Margaret [Cochrane?]; lawful children [[Glasgow-3590|Katherine]] and [Androw?/Andrew]. The death month is March, but the year is unresolved. The index says Hirmenschelis; the place is unclear in the present manuscript reading. See [[Space:1577 Glasgw, Johne|the detailed working transcription]].''
* [[Glasgow-3613|Margaret Glasgow]], apparently died December 1578; confirmed 8 November 1580
** ''Sometime wife of [[Edstoun-3|John Easton]] in Croftmalloch; [[Edstoun-4|Cuthbert Kaddell/Keddell]] is expressly her son. The record does not identify his father.''
* [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow]], will made 6 February 1597/8; died 7 February; confirmed 10 July 1598
** ''Of [Corsoun?] in Calder Cleir; wife Elizat Stevinsoun; Robert expressly their son; daughters Marion, Janet and Isobel. A further child is only a conditional provision if Elizat was pregnant.''
* Thomas
** ''1691 writer in Edinburgh''
** Possibly [[Glasgow-3187|Thomas Glasgow (bef.1627-)]] ?

These records show livestock-and-grain estates, rent and wage debts, household goods and, in Andrew's case, succession to a rural landholding. They establish three nuclear relationships but do not prove that the John, Margaret and Andrew households were siblings or branches of the Glasgow burgh pedigree.

=== Margaret Glasgow of Croftmalloch: detailed reading ===

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%; background:#f8fff8; border:2px solid #8DB600;"
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Direct genealogical result
|-
| '''[[Glasgow-3613|Margaret Glasgow]] was the mother of [[Edstoun-4|Cuthbert Kaddell/Keddell]].''' The record calls him ''hir sone'', later ''sone to the said umquhile Margaret'', and calls Margaret ''his mother''. Margaret was the sometime wife of [[Edstoun-3|John Easton]], but the record does not identify Cuthbert's father.
|}

The Edinburgh Commissary Court testament-dative and inventory is NRS '''CC8/8/8, images 355–356'''. Margaret's entry begins in the lower part of the first image and continues into the confirmation on the second; the upper part of the first image belongs to the preceding estate. Margaret died ''ab intestato''—without a will—in '''December, apparently 1578'''. The appointment decree appears dated '''[16?] October 1580''', and the clear marginal confirmation date is '''8 November 1580'''. The 1580 date is therefore not her date of death.<ref name="Margaret1580Detail">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/8, images 355–356, testament dative and inventory of Margaret Glasgow; working transcription of the original register images. Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108].</ref>

The opening family clause reads in part:

: The testament dative & inventar of the guidis, geir, soumes of money & dettis pertening to umquhile '''Margaret Glasgw''', sumtyme spous to '''Johne Estoun''' in [Croftmelloch?] … quha deceissit ab intestato in the moneth of December, the zeir of God jᵐ vᶜ [lxxviij?] … gevin up be '''Cuthbart Kaddell''' in [Croftmelloch?], '''hir sone''', executour dative surrogate …

The confirmation repeats the relationship independently:

: … the said '''Cuthbert Keddell, sone to the said umquhile Margaret''' …
:
: … confirmis the said '''Cuthbert Keddell in executour dative to the said umquhile Margaret Glasgw, his mother''' …

The spelling '''Croftmalloch''' is supplied by the published index rather than silently expanded from the difficult manuscript hand. Likewise, the son's surname is preserved in both manuscript forms, '''Kaddell''' and '''Keddell'''; it should not be converted to Easton merely because Margaret had been John Easton's wife.

==== Margaret's estate account ====

Margaret's inventory includes two cows, two one-year-old heifers, sheep including ''hoggis'' or young sheep, six bolls of oats in the barn and barnyard, household utensils and furnishings, and her clothing. Several individual livestock quantities and prices remain unresolved, but the aggregate figures are unusually clear and reconcile:

{| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding:5px; width:100%;"
|-
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Account
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Amount
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Evidence note
|-
| Goods and possessions || £47 14s 8d || Inventory total
|-
| Debts receivable || £10 10s || James Estoun in Wester Quhitburne owed £8; [Michaell Mertyn?] apparently owed 50s
|-
| '''Gross estate''' || '''£58 4s 8d''' || Inventory plus debts receivable
|-
| Debt payable || £1 || Owed to Roland Dundas in an entry concerning a year's ''teind'' or tithe
|-
| '''Net estate''' || '''£57 4s 8d''' || Gross estate less 20s
|-
| Recorded deceased's portion || £28 12s 4d || One half of the net estate
|}

James Easton and the tentatively read Michael Mertyn appear as debtors, not stated relatives. The possible cautioner's name in the later formula also remains unresolved. The secure family conclusion depends on the three explicit mother–son phrases, not on those account names or on Cuthbert's executor appointment alone.

=== Andrew Glasgow of [Corsoun?]: detailed reading ===

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%; background:#f8fff8; border:2px solid #8DB600;"
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Direct genealogical result
|-
| '''[[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow]] named Elizat Stevinsoun as his wife and expressly identified Robert Glasgow as their son.''' He also named daughters Marion, Janet and Isobel. His provision for a child with whom Elizat might be pregnant is conditional and does not prove that another child was born.
|}

This testament-testamentar and inventory is NRS '''CC8/8/32, images 123–124'''. Andrew lived at a place provisionally read as '''[Corsoun?]''' in the parish of '''[Calder Clair/Cleir]''', within the sheriffdom of Edinburgh. He made the will on '''6 February 1597''' as written, died on '''7 February''', and was confirmed on '''10 July 1598'''. Because the official Scottish year then began on 25 March, the February dates are conventionally recorded as '''1597/8'''; this adjusts the year numbering, not the calendar day.<ref name="Andrew1598Detail">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw; working transcription of the original register images. Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108]. See also [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/help-and-support/guides/dates-numbers-and-sums-money Scotland's People, “Dates, numbers and sums of money”].</ref>

The strongest parentage clause reads:

: First, he nomis '''Elizat Stevinsoun his spous and Robart Glasgw his sone, begottin be him vpoun the said Elizat his wyff''', to intromet with his guidis and geir and moveabill dettis awin to him, and to pay his dettis awin be him to vtheris.

''Elizat'' is the manuscript form and probably represents Elizabeth; it should remain visible in research notes. ''Stevinsoun'', ''his spous'' and the parentage wording are clearer. James Stevisoun appears among the named advisers whose counsel Elizat and Robert were to use, but the testament does not state whether he was her father, brother or another relative.

==== Andrew's possessions and accounts ====

The inventory appears to include three cows with calves valued at £8 each, two yearling cattle, two horses valued at £10 each or £20 together, nine sheep, eight bolls of oats in the barn and barnyard, four firlots of barley, household utensils and furnishings, and Andrew's clothing. The number of cows and several valuations remain tentative, and neither the inventory total nor the debt totals have been securely transcribed.

Among the people apparently owing Andrew money are John Mure, a person described as the widow of a deceased John whose full name remains unclear, and James Stevisoun. The debts owed by Andrew include an item for a brown horse and entries involving David Lyoun, James Stevisoun and a laird tentatively read as [Westhall?]. These financial names are research leads, not evidence of kinship.

==== Distribution, land and the children ====

After debts, Andrew directed that the free estate be divided into three parts: one third to Elizat and a second third to Robert. For Andrew's own third he provided:

: … incais his said spous be with bairne to him, the samin sall [pass?] to the said bairne. And gif scho be not with bairne, that his said thrid be deuidit equallie betuix his said sone and his said [word beginning ''dochter…'', struck through] '''Marione, Jonet, Isobell'''.

The named women are therefore Andrew's daughters, although the same explicit maternal wording used for Robert is not repeated for them. No profile should be created for the merely possible unborn child.

Andrew further directed that Elizat should ''bruik his [word unclear] land quhill his said Robart cum to aige'', after which the holding was to pass to Robert. This establishes intended succession within Andrew's household and shows that Robert had not attained the relevant age or majority. It does not establish whether the land was heritable or tenanted, from whom Andrew obtained it, or any descent from the Glasgow burgh family.

The will also provides that, if ''Elizat his spous do not hir pairt to his said bairnis'', she was to be removed from the administration. The closing notarial formula indicates that the notary signed at Andrew's direction because Andrew could not write. The remaining execution and confirmation formula is only partly resolved.

The current profile candidates for Robert, Marion, Janet and Isobel remain identity hypotheses, not established matches. The strongest next evidence would be a Caldercleir estate rental, tack, transfer, marriage or later testament carrying the Corsoun residence, Stevenson connection or Andrew-to-Robert succession into another record.

=== Katherine Glasgow and the minor Weir executors ===

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%; background:#f8fff8; border:2px solid #8DB600;"
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Direct and probable genealogical result
|-
| ✅ '''[[Glasgow-1495|Katherine Glasgow]] was the wife of [[Weir-4172|Thomas Weir]] in Stevenston parish and died in January 1603.''' 🟡 Thomas submitted her estate in the names of '''William, James and probably Jonet/Janet Weir'''; the court describes all three executors as minors. They were very probably the couple's children, but the surviving wording does not expressly call them sons, daughter or ''bairns''.
|}

Katherine's testament dative is NRS '''CC9/7/4, images 6–7'''. Her entry begins at the bottom of image 6 and ends before another testament begins at the bottom of image 7. It is an intestate estate administration, not a personal will or marriage record. The manuscript confirmation day appears to read '''[26?] May 1605''', whereas Grant's printed calendar and the Findmypast transcript give '''9 May 1605'''. The secure conclusion is confirmation in '''May 1605'''; the exact day remains unresolved.<ref name="Katherine1605Detail">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/4, images 6–7, testament dative and inventory of Katherine Glasgow; original register working transcription. Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'' (Edinburgh, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FWILLS%2F057453&tab=this Findmypast SCOT/WILLS/057453].</ref>

Her inventory names two grey horses, an old black nag, two cows, a farrow cow, bere or barley, oats and fodder, household contents and clothing. No debts owed to her were recorded. Rent to James, Earl of Glencairn, teind grain to Mr Alexander Campbell, minister at Stevenston, other private debts and servants' wages left the estate insolvent: ''Et sic debita excedunt bona''—“and thus the debts exceed the assets”—with ''Quota nulla'' in the margin. A separate creditor, John Weir in an unresolved ''Nether …'' locality, is a possible relative but is not called one. Robert Chirnsyde of Over Possill confirmed the estate, and John Crawford in Glen acted as cautioner; those official roles do not imply kinship.

'''Full record page:''' [[Space:Kathereine Glasgow: Will and testament translation|working transcription, modern-English rendering and research analysis]].

== Saltcoats maritime household ==

John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats within Ardrossan parish, died in December 1636. His widow '''Isobell Gray''' submitted the estate for his lawful children '''Katherine and Agnes Glasgow'''. Another Saltcoats sailor, John Brown, owed money to the estate and acted as cautioner; no kinship is stated. The inventory may describe an old fishing boat and equipment, but that reading remains tentative. See [[Space:John Glasgw's Testament Testamentar 1637|the working transcription and analysis]].
